criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The register is a real invention and it holds: I looked for a cast shadow on all nine and found none, depth is carried by occlusion and density only, and nothing in the 13-entry ledger is lit from behind. Four frames are genuinely drawn. Slide 4's curl is the best passage in the deck, a continuous backlight falloff from tan to near-black that reads as paper lifting off glass and never as a drop shadow. Slide 3's lattice really foreshortens (top row pitch ~110px, bottom row ~112px at 2x the ellipse size) and light-through-holes is unambiguous. Slide 5's fibre visibly crowds into a denser ring around the cut. Slide 6's polarity flip is the deck's best idea and I can read both 'will' slots at 432px. Against that: (1) the detail budget is AGAIN front loaded against the argument, deck 13's avoid_next line no. 1 in a new costume. The argument lands on 7, 8, 9 and those are the three least drawn frames: slide 7's bands are 0.088/0.088/0.061 with 6% of bottom-third cells carrying craft, slide 8 is twenty keyline rectangles over a 435px-tall completely featureless void between y=910 and y=1340, slide 9 is one filled rect, one dashed rect and a navy band. (2) FOUR of nine declared value structures are contradicted by the pixels. Slide 2's focal is 'the left window ... the frame's LIGHT EXTREME' and the gap between the wedge segments is mid khaki, while the cream bed around it is far lighter. Slide 8's focal is 'the leaf field ... carrying the frame's light extreme' and the leaves (#C9CBB0) are DARKER than the bed (#EFECD8). Slide 4's declared light extreme, 'the flush portion of the sheet', is darker than the bed surrounding it. Worst, slide 9's focal is 'the open registration area ... the brightest region in all nine frames' and between the seated leaf (x=630) and the dashed leaf (x=920) there is nothing but ordinary hatched bed at the same value as the whole frame. That region was not drawn. It is in the dossier and in no drawing step, which is deck 13's avoid_next line no. 3 verbatim, on the closing frame. (3) Slide 7's '1100 grain marks' floor is vacuously satisfied: I can find about a dozen specks in the lower two thirds at 2160px and none at 432px, so the dead sheet is a flat near-black rectangle, which is the redaction reading its own risk list named and which the 2026-08-27 avoid_next line forbids by name. (4) Slide 2 renders as the bar pair its own structure note said it was avoiding, two unequal blocks with a bright gap, and the 21 steps band into a near-smooth ramp at 432px, the exact risk that dossier wrote down. (5) Slide 6, the thesis frame, is three flat colour bands and type, its slots have machine-clean rectangular corners in a deck where every other opening is torn, and both slots abut the next word with zero space, so it sets 'willsupport' and 'willbe'. (6) Slide 9's pins render as a navy bar with a cream ellipse stuck to its upper right, extending below the sheet edge; it does not read as a pin through a hole and it is the one object slide 8's empty stations exist to pay off.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Not my lens and I found nothing I can call fabricated. computed.json carries three values each with a stated rounding rule, 68.1 is computed and slide 2 asserts it never appears, 12 and 8 are never summed and the string '20' is forbidden on slide 8, and 10.4 million and more than 10 million are printed with separate attributions inside one opening with an assertion that no element holds both. Slide 8's absence names the document it is missing from. Two deductions. First, slide 4's second dek sentence, 'No meeting date is published for that approval.', is the deck's own fairness obligation and it is in the DOM and not on the page (see hard_fails), so an absence the run treats as load-bearing does not reach a reader. Second, slide 2's wedge encodes both figures by POSITION with no origin and no scale stated: the measured block runs x=180 to 980 and the peak tick sits at x=1390 in a field ending at 1510, which is 61.7% and 91.0% of the span against a true ratio of 68.1%. A reader reading distance off that ramp is reading an encoding the frame does not define, and the dossier's own risk note ('a reader could take the distance between the windows to mean petaflops were lost') is what the render now invites. Flagging both for the integrity judge rather than claiming a fabricated numeral.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader gets it: rank 66, two System pages in the future tense, the machine's own documentation in the present tense saying invitation-only controlled beta, and onboarding expected with no date. It is fair rather than a gotcha, and slides 4 and 8 carry that fairness as the storyboard promised. Slide 9 names the deciding body (TAMUS governance) and prints 'No date is published for it' rather than inventing one, which is the right call. But the rubric's 9 wants a county, a body and a deadline, and this deck has one of three by the record's own limits. What a Texan can DO with it is thin, essentially watch for an onboarding announcement, and the caption's closing question ('Which of the twelve universities have?') hands them a question rather than a step. Slide 4's lost line costs the fairness half a little of its weight.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: There is a real turn and it is legible on the strip without reading a word: frames 1 to 6 sit mid, frame 7 drops to a dead bed, and 8 and 9 come back up on the shared registration rail. The cover earns a swipe. The problems are that the deck nominates its own cuttable frame (slide 3) and is right, since 3 and 5 are the same object twice and 3 carries inventory rather than argument, and that the momentum peak at 7 lands on the deck's least drawn frame, so the moment a reader is most engaged is the moment the art is thinnest. Slide 2 is skippable in a way nothing at position 2 should be.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: The hooks are written by somebody: 'Count the holes. There are 95.', 'Read the verb.', 'Not one of them is punched.' No em dashes, no first person outside a quotation, straight quotes in the caption. But the rubric asks for regional specificity over state-level abstraction and this deck has neither region nor really state. The palette note admits it may not put the story on the ground, and the result is nine frames that would read identically about a university system in any state. 'Post Oak Savannah sand horizon' is claimed in the token table and is invisible to a reader as anything but khaki. And the deck's quotation code is inconsistent on slide 7: 'FEATURES AND TOOLS ARE EVOLVING; BETA MAY NOT GUARANTEE FULL SUPPORT OR CAPACITY' carries a semicolon and is set in the same mono furniture voice as 'DOCS.VISION.TAMUS.EDU', with no quotation marks and no attribution, while slides 4 and 6 both mark their quotes. The verbatim carve-out probably saves the semicolon, but nothing on the frame tells a reader it is a quotation.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The headline is genuinely new against the 14-entry window: no prior deck is lit from behind, none has zero cast shadows, and no prior carries a diazo blueline palette. Three familiar moves against that. Backlit knockout through opaque material is deck no. 9's technique from 2026-08-27, inside the window ('letterforms cut clean through a steel plate and backlit'), and it carries three of this deck's nine frames (3, 5, 6). raw #F2EFD6 is a near miss of deck 7's bond #F2EEE4 and deck 13's bond #EFE9DC, which is precisely the collision class the 2026-08-28 entry recorded and asked for a perceptual check on, and it is this deck's most-seen colour. 'N identical objects asserted identical because the record ranks nobody' is now three decks running: 12's 28 bodies, 13's three plates, this deck's 20 leaves. Distinct, with more than one familiar move.

hard_fails: UNFINISHED FRAME, slide 4. The dek overflows its sepia plate and its second sentence, 'No meeting date is published for that approval.', renders in cream on the cream bed below the sheet at roughly 1.05 to 1 contrast, with the torn edge of the curl cutting across the tops of the glyphs. It is a ghost at 2160px and it is entirely absent at 432px, where I cannot detect it at all. The acceptance item 'the dek says No meeting date is published, because the record found none' passes because the string is in the DOM. This is the failure mode already written into the 2026-08-21 ledger entry as a structural law, 'a container's edge is not its content's edge', recurring on the frame that carries the deck's fairness.
one_sentence_fix: Every acceptance item in this deck asserts a string, a count or a node and not one of them measures whether a mark or a word is VISIBLE against the ground it actually lands on, which is why an illegible sentence on slide 4, an invisible 1100-mark grain field on slide 7 and an undrawn 16-percent focal region on slide 9 all shipped with zero machine QA fails, so the next run's per-frame assertions must compute contrast ratio against the sampled local background for every text node and a measured value delta for every declared focal AREA, and throw below the floor.
